name: verified-index-still-races-the-commit
description: "git diff --cached passing immediately before commit does not protect you; the window between check and commit is only closed by a private index, re-seeded in the same shell call"
metadata:

---

`git add <explicit paths>` then `git diff --cached --name-status` showing
**exactly** your files, then `git commit` — and the commit contains another
lane's file instead of yours. Measured 2026-07-29 (run 0086, AJC): commit
`c752d200f2` carries my message over an AJCR lane's 172-line
`Pic0ChartVMonotone.lean`; my own two paths were absent. Both checks were
truthful when they ran and stale by the time `commit` read the index.

**Why:** the workspace-recommended guard (`I-1070`: "diff --cached before
committing") closes the wrong window. The gap is between *verification* and
*commit*, not between *add* and *verification* — so no amount of checking before
the commit helps. This is the additive twin of the staged-*deletion* hazard
(`I-1041`, `I-1055`); nothing is lost, but authorship is silently wrong, and the
file's real author sees their work land under a message about something else.

**How to apply:** commit through a private index, and do the whole sequence in
**one** shell invocation, because `GIT_INDEX_FILE` does not survive between tool
calls:

```bash
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/idx-$$ && G() { git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" \
  --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" "$@"; } && \
  G read-tree HEAD && G add -- <your paths> && G diff --cached --name-status HEAD && \
  G commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
...
MSG
```

Two further traps measured the same session. (1) `read-tree HEAD` goes stale
too: if HEAD advances while you build, the commit guard refuses with "would
DELETE N tracked files you did not change" — that refusal is *correct*, and the
fix is to re-seed against the new HEAD, never
`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1`. (2) A commit reporting "no changes added"
can mean your edits **already reached HEAD** inside another lane's integrate
sweep; check `git log --oneline -- <path>` and read the HEAD blob before
re-doing the work. See [[commit-with-pathspec-not-index]] for the deletion side,
and [[uncommitted-work-reaches-head-via-other-lanes]].
